### Electron Version

macOS

### Operating System Version

15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

36.0.0-beta.6

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When invoking `showSaveDialog()` with the following, the "Save As" edit box should show "Untitled.cpp".

```javascript
    dialog.showSaveDialog({
      title: "Save Untitled1",
      defaultPath: homedir(),
      buttonLabel: 'Save',
      filters: [
        {name: 'C++', extensions: ['cpp']},
        {name: 'All Files', extensions: ['*']}
      ]
    })
```

### Actual Behavior

On macOS only, it shows "Untitled.cp", dropping the second "p". This worked up until 36.0.0-beta.6, breaking in beta.7.

https://gist.github.com/c8e8887474637708a8ce7023f7d99d6b

Ubuntu

22.04

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

 It is necessary to clearly specify how to install it  in document.

### Actual Behavior

1: document guide
according to https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/installation#cache As mentioned above, the cache directory is stored in the form of [checksum]/[filename],
So if I want to install v35.0.1 offline on Ubuntu, my cache directory should be "~/ cache/electron/96ee99e61ef0a727915e763cf18a5c83536fbf7855702ce47d4d06e971e40d01/electron-v35.0.1-linux-x64.zip",
96ee99e61ef0a727915e763cf18a5c83536fbf7855702ce47d4d06e971e40d01 is from SHASUMS256.txt.
But in reality, it's not possible

2: install debug
debug the code node_modules/@electron/get/dist/cjs/Cache.js

```
strippedUrl='https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v35.0.1'
crypto
            .createHash('sha256')
            .update(strippedUrl)
            .digest('hex');
```
so found should put in cache directory like below:
"~/ cache/electron/1dafae12d714b3c9cdf2dd18c3b8e737927d09477e3f6712bd0c4b77bc87f428/electron-v35.0.1-linux-x64.zip"

Why is the document inconsistent with the actual situation？

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Accelerator null on predefined menu roles
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.1.0 and below

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When getting the menu via Menu.getApplicationMenu(), the accelerators should not be null for the predefined menu roles such as copy, paste, etc.

### Actual Behavior

Any menu items with a user-defined accelerator correctly returns the accelerator, but any of the predefined menu roles such as undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, etc. return null for the accelerator, despite those accelerators being registered and working.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/johnbwoodruff/725227db5ae734f73de6efd3af2a7960

### Additional Information

I had previously opened an issue for this, #34705, but it was closed due to no activity.

The accelerators are definitely defined for these predefined roles. The hotkeys work correctly, and they're displayed when the native menu is rendered. However, if you want to render your own custom menu, you won't know those accelerators as they are returned as `null`.

You can see in https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/5af6b898d92432369ce9495e75d75b02af651531/lib/browser/api/menu-item-roles.ts#L36-L41, for example, that all of these roles have accelerators properly defined. (hence why they work when you use them) So those accelerators should come through on the menu when using `Menu.getApplicationMenu()`.

I believe the fix should be here: https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/lib/browser/api/menu-item.ts#L28

Specifically like so:

```this.overrideReadOnlyProperty('accelerator', roles.getDefaultAccelerator(this.role));```

I was going to submit a PR for this fix but I wasn't able to get the build environment working on my laptop so I couldn't properly validate the fix and I didn't want to submit a spam PR that hasn't followed the contribution guidelines.

nodes.title: Electron-based apps cause a huge system-wide lag on macOS 26
nodes.body:
### Maintainer update

From @MarshallOfSound (https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48311#issuecomment-3304577581):

> Hey folks, anyone experiencing this issue can you please raise a Feedback (via Feedback Assistant) with Apple. Make sure you send it while the issue is occurring and ensure you include a sysdiagnose with your report (I think that's automatic now, but check the box if there's a box).
> 
> We need a lot more to go on and this is likely a macOS issue.

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.3.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26 Tahoe RC

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A, issue only persists since macOS 26

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Smooth 120fps experience even when Electron-apps are open or not minimized

### Actual Behavior

Using an M1 Max MacBook Pro, having Electron-based apps open / not minimized causes a huge lag.
CPU and GPU usage remains low, but if I have Discord and VS Code open, moving windows, scrolling is stuttery. It happens even when only Discord is open but it gets worse if I open a second Electron app.
This is kind of weird because while having Discord open and I'm in Chrome, the lag still occurs, but it's fixed if I minimize Discord (even though Chrome is fully in focus and maximized). This happens since upgrading to macOS 26 RC, macOS 15 didn't have this issue.
There is a similar lag if I open Settings - Wallpapers, moving the Settings window is laggy then (looks like 60fps instead of 120).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Print dialog on macOS does not show preview and page count is incorrect when using `window.print()` with `page-break-after`
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

34.3.4,38.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Sequoia

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When calling `window.print()`, the macOS system print dialog should:  
1. Display a preview thumbnail on the left.  
2. Show the correct number of pages as defined by the HTML content (with CSS pagination such as `page-break-after`).  

### Actual Behavior

When calling `window.print()` in Electron on macOS Sequoia:  
- The print dialog opens without a preview thumbnail on the left.  
- The page count is incorrect — it does not match the actual expected number of pages when using `page-break-after` in the HTML.  

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/lsiten/9d6cf094167aacb7575df7e10f8b41c7

### Additional Information

1. Open the provided example Electron application.  
2. Click the **"Print Document"** button in the rendered window.  
3. Observe the macOS print dialog:  
   - No preview thumbnail displayed on the left.  
   - Page count does not match expected value.  
**Testcase ZIP:**  

[electron-demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22289046/electron-demo.zip)

nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version Tested in (35, 37) and an unknown version ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Issue found on Arch Linux + Windows ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior Rendered the emoji/kaomoji correctly e.g. (;ﾟ∇ﾟ) if the system worked correctly the following text should look like (;ﾟ∇ﾟ) a(;ﾟ∇ﾟ) ### Actual Behavior Some emoji/Kaomoji are rendered incorrect if they do not contain another character in front of them. the following text: (;ﾟ∇ﾟ) a(;ﾟ∇ﾟ) looks like this ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Recently I was sent some text on discord that showed the corrupted characters which when pointed out the sender stated that it works fine on the android version but on the desktop version don't render correctly. This originally led me to believe it was due to a missing font on my PC. However, when I was editing the text in VSCode I noticed that if I added any charactered to the beginning of it the text would then start rendering correctly. which I pasted back into discord with an additional character all users were able to view the text correctly. Non electron apps do not show this behavior e.g. Kate (KDE text editor), windows Notepad

### Description

@codebytere and @ckerr discovered that Electron uses Chromium's views API incorrectly.

They added a patch (TODO: which one?) to revert a Chromium change to fix #47536.

They said that this will be a longer refactor to use the Chromium views API properly.

@codebytere agreed during the WG Releases call on August 20, 2025 to fill in the technical details on this issue:

- [ ] Describe how we're using the API incorrectly
- [ ] Describe the refactor that would be necessary
- [ ] Link to the patch we're floating

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

38.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown; reproduces back to v36 at least

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Calling:
```js
app.relaunch()
app.quit()
```
should restart the app, regardless of how it's launched.

### Actual Behavior

If the application is launched by double-clicking on the executable within the built app, it restarts correctly.

If however, the built application is launched by running the executable from the command line, using a `.desktop` file; or the app is run unbuilt via `electron .`, the `relaunch()` call appears to have no effect, and the app simply quits and does not restart.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/ExodusMovement/electron-ubuntu-restart-minimal-repro

### Additional Information

Worth noting that due to https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/42510, it is necessary to `chown root` and `chmod 4755` the `chrome-sandbox` file before running from the command line. Oddly, a built application that has not had anything done to `chrome-sandbox` can be run by double-clicking the binary (in which case restarting also works); not sure if there's some connection there.

nodes.title: Electron window loses its snapped state when restored from minimized
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro, version 24H2, OS build 26100

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

1. Snap an Electron app window to one side of the screen on Windows 11 using Snap Layouts or Snap Assist.
2. Snap a second window (could be notepad.exe or any other native apps) to the other side to form a Snap Group.
3. Minimize the snapped Electron window.
4. Restore it from the taskbar.
5. The window should: 
  5.1 Remain in the snapped / arranged state
  5.2 The Snap Group’s shared splitter between the two windows should remain active, allowing simultaneous resizing of both windows.

### Actual Behavior

1. After restoring, the Electron window remains in the correct position and size, but it is no longer part of the Snap Group. (In 37.4.0, the four window corners remain right angles, but the window is not in snap state anymore)
2. The shared split-bar is gone, so resizing one window no longer affects the other.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This issue reopens https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/48122 which is not fully addressed in 37.4.0

I wrote a demo electron app to check if the window is in snap state, hope it helps.

https://github.com/arshcaria/electron_snap
